bug_description.normalized: The staged 1413-byte witness is accepted by `hb_face_create()` as an sfnt font whose table directory contains `fvar`, `glyf`, `gvar`, `loca`, and `maxp`. Later table reads recover `maxp.numGlyphs == 4`, `fvar.axisCount == gvar.axisCount == 1`, `gvar.dataZ == 5123`, and the final byte `0x01`, so hb-draw-fuzzer keeps `num_coords == 1` and iterates glyphs `0..3`. In that witness the gvar short-offset array decodes to `[67584, 6, 16384, 6, 67584]`, so only glyph 1 or glyph 3 can reach `OT::gvar::get_glyph_var_data()` with `start_offset == 6` and `end_offset` 16384 or 67584. The helper returns `((unsigned char *) this + start_offset) + dataZ` after only intra-offset checks and never verifies that `dataZ + [start_offset, end_offset)` stays inside the 192-byte `gvar` blob. `GlyphVarData::has_data()` then reads `tupleVarCount` through that out-of-bounds pointer, and `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()` triggers the observed 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The OSS-Fuzz issue text labels the bug as heap-use-after-free and CWE-416, but the saved ASAN reproduction for this staged sample is a heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: First non-harness statement on the crashing path. It sanitizes the attacker blob as `OT::OpenTypeFontFile` and stores the resulting parser-owned face closure that later lazy `fvar`, `maxp`, `glyf`, and `gvar` table loads all read from.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 1413-byte sfnt font whose directory places `fvar` at byte 92, `gvar` at 124, and `maxp` at 204. This call accepts that blob as a sanitized OpenType face, after which later table reads on the same closure recover `fvar.axisCount == 1`, `gvar.dataZ == 5123`, and `maxp.numGlyphs == 4`.
source.note: This is the first library statement that consumes the fuzzer bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state; the later axis-count, glyph-count, and gvar-table reads all come from this face closure.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Once the lazy gvar accelerator has loaded the table, the attacker-controlled gvar bytes contribute both the per-glyph offset pair and the base `dataZ` offset that are later added together to form the invalid `GlyphVarData` pointer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Static parsing of the staged witness yields `gvar.dataZ == 5123` and short-offset words `[0x8400, 0x0003, 0x2000, 0x0003, 0x8400]`, so the accessor can materialize candidate pairs `start_offset == 6, end_offset == 16384` for glyph 1 or `start_offset == 6, end_offset == 67584` for glyph 3.

root_cause.description: The helper converts attacker-controlled `dataZ` and per-glyph gvar offsets into a raw `GlyphVarData` pointer without checking that `dataZ + [start_offset, end_offset)` stays inside the serialized gvar blob.
root_cause.note: The fix replaces this raw-reference path with blob-bounded `hb_bytes_t` slices from `blob->as_bytes().sub_array(((unsigned) dataZ) + start_offset, length)`, so an out-of-range glyph-var span collapses to empty bytes instead of being dereferenced.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. While `GlyphVarData::has_data()` converts `tupleVarCount`, this helper reads two bytes through the out-of-bounds pointer returned by `get_glyph_var_data()`.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this exact line, with callers `OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u>::operator unsigned int() const` and `OT::GlyphVarData::has_data() const`.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker bytes are accepted as a sanitized OpenType face, so later lazy loads of `fvar`, `gvar`, and `glyf` operate on this font instead of falling back to an empty face.

gvar_shallow_sanitized.description: The witness `gvar` table survives shallow sanitization because its short-offset array makes `get_offset (0) == get_offset (glyphCount) == 67584`, so this check covers an empty span and does not reject the later glyph-1/glyph-3 ranges built from `start_offset == 6` plus `dataZ == 5123`.

evidence_limitations: Static inspection of the staged witness does recover `gvar.dataZ == 5123`, `get_offset (0) == get_offset (glyphCount) == 67584`, and the fact that only glyph 1 or glyph 3 can survive `get_glyph_var_data()`'s local checks with `start_offset == 6` and `end_offset` 16384 or 67584. Runtime disambiguation is disabled for this sample, so the remaining ambiguity is only which of those two candidate glyph arms produced the observed fault.

The ARVO metadata labels this sample as CWE-416 and heap-use-after-free, but the saved ASAN trace and the staged `reproduction_report.json` consistently show a heap-buffer-overflow read in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 1413-byte sfnt font. Static inspection finds `fvar` at byte 92, `glyf` at 108, `gvar` at 124, `head` at 140, `loca` at 188, and `maxp` at 204 in the table directory; `maxp.numGlyphs == 4`, `gvar.dataZ == 5123`, the gvar short-offset array decodes to `[67584, 6, 16384, 6, 67584]`, and the final byte is `0x01`. On the saved run, hb-draw-fuzzer uses that byte to keep `num_coords == 1`, iterates glyphs `0..3`, and only glyph 1 or glyph 3 can reach `get_glyph_var_data()` with `start_offset == 6`, so `has_data()` crashes in the 2-byte read at `hb.hh:541`.

format.name: OpenType variable-font blob for hb-draw-fuzzer
format.contract: Use the exact staged 1413-byte witness. It must preserve `fvar.axisCount == gvar.axisCount == 1`, `maxp.numGlyphs == 4`, the final byte `0x01`, `gvar.dataZ == 5123`, and the short-offset words `[0x8400, 0x0003, 0x2000, 0x0003, 0x8400]`. Those exact fields make the harness keep `num_coords == 1`, iterate glyphs `0..3`, and give only glyph 1 or glyph 3 a locally accepted gvar range with `start_offset == 6` and `end_offset` 16384 or 67584, after which `get_glyph_var_data()` returns the out-of-bounds `this + dataZ + start_offset` pointer that `has_data()` dereferences.

fine_trace.note: Harness setup step. The 1413-byte witness is turned into a HarfBuzz face object; static byte inspection shows a variable-font directory containing `fvar`, `gvar`, and `maxp`, and the final input byte is `0x01`.

Source step. This is the first non-harness statement on the crashing path that consumes the attacker bytes. It sanitizes the witness as an OpenType font and packages the accepted blob into the face closure later used by lazy table loads.
The harness queries the sanitized face's `fvar` table and reads `axisCount == 1`, the upper bound later used to clamp the number of variation coordinates.

The harness materializes the final attacker-controlled byte into the local coordinate-count candidate. For the staged witness that byte is `0x01`, so `num_coords` becomes 1 before the clamp against step 3's axis count.
The harness clamps the attacker-selected coordinate count against the font's axis count. With step 3 returning 1 and step 4 already holding 1, the final `num_coords` stays 1.

The font object adopts exactly one normalized variation coordinate. The actual coordinate value is not needed to trigger this bug; what matters is that `font->num_coords` is now nonzero and equals the table axis count.
The harness's `hb_face_get_glyph_count (face)` request reaches `load_num_glyphs()` and reads `maxp.numGlyphs == 4` from the sanitized face.
The harness stores the face glyph count. With step 7 returning 4 and the next line clamping `glyph_count` to at most 16, the loop bound remains 4 and the draw loop will cover glyph IDs `0..3`.

With loop bound 4, the harness draws glyph IDs `0..3`. Static recovery of the gvar offsets shows only the `i == 1` or `i == 3` iteration can survive the later local offset checks; runtime disambiguation is disabled, so the staged artifacts do not distinguish which of those two calls crashed.

fine_trace.code: if (unlikely (!face->table.gvar->apply_deltas_to_points (gid, font->coords, font->num_coords, points.as_array ()))) return false;
fine_trace.note: During glyph drawing, this is the first draw-path dereference of the lazy `face->table.gvar` loader. It requests gvar deltas for the selected `gid` with `font->num_coords == 1`, which forces the gvar accelerator to be created before `apply_deltas_to_points()` runs.

Triggered by step 10's lazy-loader access, `init()` reads the attacker-controlled `gvar` table from the sanitized face and compares it against `fvar`. Because the crash path continues instead of calling `fini()`, the witness keeps `gvar_table->axisCount == axis_count == 1`, `gvar_table->glyphCount == face->get_num_glyphs () == 4`, and `dataZ == 5123`. The comment at line 400 also states that per-glyph `GlyphVarData` is not sanitized here and must be checked while accessing each glyph.

The variation gate keeps `coord_count == 1`. Because `gvar_table->axisCount` is also 1, the following early-return condition `!coord_count || coord_count != gvar_table->axisCount` is false, so HarfBuzz proceeds to fetch glyph variation data instead of bailing out.

The attacker-controlled gvar short-offset array words `[0x8400, 0x0003, 0x2000, 0x0003, 0x8400]` decode to byte offsets `[67584, 6, 16384, 6, 67584]`. For the harness's four glyphs, only glyph 1 and glyph 3 produce locally acceptable ranges (`start_offset == 6`, `end_offset` 16384 or 67584); glyphs 0 and 2 reverse the order and are rejected by the later guard.

Root cause. The same attacker-controlled gvar header contributes `dataZ == 5123`, so after only checking that the selected offsets are non-empty and at least `GlyphVarData::min_size` wide, the helper returns `this + dataZ + start_offset`. For either candidate glyph from step 13 that means a pointer starting at byte `5129` in a serialized `gvar` blob whose staged length is only 192 bytes, yet the code never checks that `dataZ + [start_offset, end_offset)` stays inside the blob. The patch restores exactly that missing obligation with `blob->as_bytes().sub_array(...)`.
The returned pointer is immediately reinterpreted as a `GlyphVarData` object and HarfBuzz asks for its first 2-byte field `tupleVarCount` to decide whether the glyph has variation data.
ASAN sink. Converting `tupleVarCount` from step 15 performs the observed 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow read through the out-of-bounds pointer created at step 14.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fix replaces raw `GlyphVarData` references with blob-bounded `hb_bytes_t` slices in the gvar access path, including the `apply_deltas_to_points()` caller that the saved crash stack reaches.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved ASAN stack is `BEInt -> IntType -> GlyphVarData::has_data -> gvar::accelerator_t::apply_deltas_to_points -> glyf::Glyph::get_points -> hb_font_draw_glyph`; fine-trace steps 10 through 16 reconstruct the glyf-side `face->table.gvar` access that triggers lazy init as a side effect, then the one-axis gate, candidate-glyph offset decoding, `dataZ`-based raw-pointer creation, and the crashing read immediately around those frames.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The attacker font controls the one-axis gate plus `gvar.dataZ == 5123` and the short-offset array `[67584, 6, 16384, 6, 67584]`; once the coord-count guard is bypassed, glyph 1 or glyph 3 supplies `start_offset == 6`, `get_glyph_var_data()` returns `this + 5129`, and `tupleVarCount` is read through that pointer at the crash site.
